I'm not really even sure why anyone even talks about The Verge anymore. At their absolute peak they were simply an also-ran, perhaps getting a review or story posted before better sites (like Anandtech) put out the definitive article. Since that time, they've fallen off a cliff in terms of the quality of their content, not that it was really that great to begin with either.

I can see where their logic came from, they understood that Apple was doing something right with the whole "lifestyle" branding and craved the dollar per customer ratio they saw attached to that ideal. Unfortunately for them, this approach really works best when you are selling physical goods. Staring reality in the face, they doubled down on their efforts and dumbed down further.

This point was really driven home when one of the higher ups at The Verge was on This Week In Tech a few months ago (I want to say it was around February or so, but it could have been last Fall). He told Leo LaPorte that his model of "bits and bauds" couldn't draw an audience any longer and that The Verge was going to succeed on a great scale by leaving all of the actual quantitative facts out of their product and rely more on qualitative aspects (in different words of course, I'm just going off memory here).

You can imagine how this went over with the panel (which included the OG Trollmaster John C Dvorak), essentially like a fart in church. They moved on, but the fellow was generally in a foul mood for the rest of the podcast. To make this even worse, it isn't like he said this to one of the masters of finer details (like the aforementioned Anand Lal Shimpi who is severely missed in journalism). These guys just simply "don't get it" and won't be missed when they are gone.
